title: St Norberts Church
description: In 1956 Cardinal O’Hara, then Archbishop of Philadelphia, formed a new parish, St. Norbert, from portions of St. Monica’s in Berwyn and St. Patrick’s in Malvern. He entrusted its care to the Norbertines. The pastor of St. Norbert Parish is nominated by the Abbot of Daylesford Abbey. The founding pastor of the parish was Father Robert L. Hyde. He celebrated the first parish Mass at 7:00 AM on Sunday, July 15, 1956 in the old Paoli Fire House. - Roger Thorne

title: Cleaver’s Store
description: Caption: I. A. Cleaver’s general store in Berwyn about 1900. Berwyn, like other towns along the Main Line, was initially established along the old Lancaster Turnpike and Conestoga Road used by thousands of travelers throughout the eighteenth century as the main road westward.  By the late nineteenth century, businesses such as Cleaver’s often continued to serve the new settlements spurred on by the growth and success of the railroads.

title: Devon Inn
description: Caption: The Devon Inn, inspired by the quick success of the Bryn Mawr Hotel, was built in an effort to appeal to Philadelphias wealthiest citizens as a summer resort.  After the first building was destroyed less than a year after its completion, the inn seen here was built, in 1884.  The Devon Horse Show was conceived and initially held on the grounds of the inn in 1896.  The building was later acquired by the Valley Forge Military Academy in 1928.  As before, less than a year after it changed hands, the inn was destroyed by fire.
source: Historic Photos of the Mainline by Laura Beardsley, © 2008 Turner Publishing Company

title: Lancaster Avenue, Devon

title: President Calvin Coolidge at the Devon Horse Show
description: Caption: President Calvin Coolidge (at center) with his wife and several members of the Main Line community are shown attending the Devon Horse Show on May 30, 1922.  First held in 1896, the Devon Horse Show is the oldest and largest outdoor multi-breed horse show in the nation. Original interest in establishing the show grew from the important role of horses in transportation as the number of large estates multiplied along the railroad line. The horse show continues to emphasize good horse breeding and training, as it did when founded.
source: Historic Photos of the Mainline by Laura Beardsley, © 2008 Turner Publishing Company

title: Diamond Rock School
description: Caption: Located near Paoli, the Diamond Rock Octagonal School built in 1818 by Mennonites as a one-room schoolhouse.  The eight sides accommodated all six grade levels, a teacher’s wall, and the door.  The teacher stood in the center of the room to address each class.  The school was restored in 1908 and is seen here in 1955.  It remains a popular summertime historic attraction.
source: Historic Photos of the Mainline by Laura Beardsley, © 2008 Turner Publishing Company

title: Easttown Elementary school
description: Caption: The new Easttown Township School opened in Berwyn in October 1932 to accomodate four hundred students in grade kindergarten through seventh.  The $235,000 building features 16 classrooms and a combined gymnasium and auditorium.

title: Great Valley Mill
description: Caption: The Great Valley Mill on Valley Road near the Paoli Station about 1920. title: Valley Creek at Upper Forge site
Diagram of Remains of Upper Forge
Upper Forge Excavation
description: “Potts-Dewees Forge.  The long lost Valley (originally Mount Joy) Forge. Due to the silting of Valley Creek, the site of the forge had been lost for over a century.  Having being rediscovered in 1929, it was dug out from over 11 feet of slit.  This was the forge belonging to Isaac Potts and William Dewees, that was burnt by the British, September 18, 1777. The forge stood between Mount Joy and Valley Forge Mountain. The photograph shows the north wall during excavation. The building was constructed of stone without mortar binding.”

title: Betzwood
description: “In the midst of a region known for its splendid tillage and beautiful vistas, Betzwood, upon the eastern shore of the Schuylkill River, opposite Port Kennedy and within sight of Valley Forge, is the most extensive and beautiful farm property. This fine tract of more than a thousand acres has been developed by Mr. John F. Betz of Philadelphia, as not only a ideal country home for himself and Mr. John F. Betz jr., but as a stock farm for the breeding of fine cattle and horses. Mr. Betz also engages here in raising of carriage, saddle, and draught horses of registered pedigrees. Betzwood includes besides its broad grazing acres, extensive well planted lawns, threaded with winding private drives, handsome modern residences, conservatories, a deer park and large power plant on the banks of the river. Betzwood station, upon the Schuylkill division of the Pennsylvania Railroad, also upon the property, is reached by frequent trains in about one hour from Broad Street station. Mr. Buck Taylor the famous frontiersman, is superintendent.” - from Valley Forge: A Chronicle of American Heroism by Frank Taylor (1905)
source: Valley Forge: A Chronicle of American Heroism by Frank Taylor (1905). Available online at Hathitrust.org

title: Beans Mineral Railway Cars
description:
View of three abandoned, partially salvaged wooden body gondola/dumper style cars at the disused Beans Quarry And Sand Company narrow gauge railroad terminal yard at the Company’s rock crusher in Valley Forge Village.
This rear view shows the car end, link and pin type coupler and the side drop doors of these cars which brought quartzite rock and sand down from the Bean Sand And Quarry Company’s quarries on Mt. Misery to the company’s rock crusher for processing and shipment via a siding on the Reading Railroad. One of the car’s trucks is visible under the rear end of the closest car.  The horizontal style handbrake application wheels at the far ends of the two more distant cars are visible in this photo. - Jim Brazel
photographer: J. Lawrence Dixon, Quaker City Railroad Society
contributor: James P. Brazel, West Jersey Chapter, National Railway Historical Society
rights: Owned by the Tredyffrin Easttown Historical Society

title: Bean Mineral Railway Locomotive
description:
Front/right quarter view of abandoned Climax Class B geared logging locomotive at the disused Beans Quarry And Sand Company narrow gauge railroad terminal yard at the Company’s rock crusher in Valley Forge Village.  At right of the photo the engine and car service facility’s water tank for supply to the steam locomotive’s water tank has been overturned from its concrete elevated foundation. 
The headlamp, round front smokebox door and most of the sheet metal sheathing on the boiler have been removed since active use. 
A photo and information on a similar Climax Class B locomotive in operating order may be found at TEHS Image Collection Identifier RR02, SN 1175.  
Research on the Climax Manufacturing Company’s production and sales indicates that a Class B locomotive of 40 tons weight was sold to Beans Sand And Quarry Company in or before the year 1915. Ref.: The Climax Locomotive, D.B. Thompson et al, 2002 Oso Publishing
. - Jim Brazel
photographer: J. Lawrence Dixon, Quaker City Railroad Society
contributor: James P. Brazel, West Jersey Chapter, National Railway Historical Society
rights: Owned by the Tredyffrin Easttown Historical Society

title: Bryn Mawr Homes
description:
Strafford Village Architectural Design Album.

This collection documents the architectural vision of the Strafford Village development located northeast of Strafford train station in Tredyffrin Township. Builder Stephan Schifter started the development in 1939 and built several homes before the start of World War II, continuing construction at the war”s conclusion. The designs of these homes are represented in the pages in this scrapbook and other loose drawings prepared by architect Harold Edward Williams. The homes depicted are examples of the revivalist styles popular in the pre-war era and include designs inspired by English, French, and Early American architecture. The documents consist of of a total of 58 sheets of plans and renderings, and one overall plot plan of the development pasted to the inside cover of the disassembled scrapbook. - Greg Prichard
rights: Owned by Tredyffrin Easttown Historical Society.

This collection documents the architectural vision of the Strafford Village development located northeast of Strafford train station in Tredyffrin Township. Builder Stephan Schifter started the development in 1939 and built several homes before the start of World War II, continuing construction at the war’s conclusion. The designs of these homes are represented in the pages in this scrapbook and other loose drawings prepared by architect Harold Edward Williams. The homes depicted are examples of the revivalist styles popular in the pre-war era and include designs inspired by English, French, and Early American architecture. The documents consist of of a total of 58 sheets of plans and renderings, and one overall plot plan of the development pasted to the inside cover of the disassembled scrapbook. - Greg Prichard
rights: Owned by Tredyffrin Easttown Historical Society.
